negative_findings.description: The session's WebSearch budget (200/200 calls) was already exhausted before this scout issued a single query, so NONE of the assigned seed queries could be run through a search engine. Fallback search endpoints were then attempted and all failed: DuckDuckGo HTML and Lite endpoints served a CAPTCHA challenge ('Select all squares containing a duck'), Mojeek returned HTTP 403, and Bing's RSS output endpoint (bing.com/search?...&format=rss) returned cache-collided results unrelated to the query — a query for '"Diebold Nixdorf" "Czech Republic" bank ATM press release' returned ten Italian-language Lionel Messi quiz pages, and vendor-name queries returned only navigational homepage results with the long-tail terms silently dropped.
negative_findings.result_summary: All discovery in this slice was therefore done by first-principles reasoning about source categories, direct URL navigation to vendor domains, redirect-chain following, and ON-SITE search endpoints (which did work — Temenos site search returned the Czech evidence). Recall is consequently structurally biased toward vendors whose domains could be guessed and away from long-tail or unexpected actors.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: This slice should be treated as high-precision but incomplete recall. A re-run of this cell with a working search budget is likely to add materially new candidates, particularly smaller vendors and Czech-language items that only a search index would surface.

negative_findings.description: Czech-language keyword search through a search engine — the mandatory cs-language leg of the method — could not be executed for the same budget reason. The Czech seed query 'Diebold Nixdorf NCR Atleos tisková zpráva Česká republika banka bankomaty' was never run. Czech-language coverage in this slice was instead achieved by navigating directly to Czech-language sources and reading them in Czech (protext.cz, bankovnictvionline.cz, systemonline.cz, lupa.cz) and by building the cs glossary from first principles.
negative_findings.result_summary: Three Czech-language sources were verified live and are included as candidates (ČTK Protext finance and IT categories, Bankovnictví online, IT Systems/SystemOnLine). Czech terms actually used against live sites: tisková zpráva, tiskové zprávy, bankomat, finance a ekonomika, IT komunikace a elektronika, vyhledávání, zprávy, banky a finance, banky a finanční organizace, přehledy, technologie, regulace, komerční přílohy, Komerční banka, Česká republika. Terms built but NOT yet exercised against any index: platební terminál, jádrový bankovní systém, samoobslužná zóna, recyklace hotovosti, výroční zpráva, případová studie, nasazení, implementace, dodavatel.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Czech-language discovery is present but shallow. Any Czech-language vendor announcement that lives outside these three portals is currently invisible to this cell.

negative_findings.description: No Czech-language edition of any global banking-technology vendor site in this cell was located. https://www.dieboldnixdorf.com/cs-cz returned HTTP 500. Comarch's finance news section explicitly offers EN/PL/DE/FR/IT/ES/PT and no Czech option, and www.comarch.cz resolved to a parked domain (certificate issued for parking.domeny.tv). Printec's Czech entry point could not be established: printecgroup.com paths returned 403 and https://www.printec.cz/ failed TLS validation with a self-signed certificate.
negative_findings.result_summary: Working hypothesis for this cell: the global vendors publish Czech-relevant material in English only, and any Czech-language version reaches the market through the ČTK Protext wire or Czech trade press rather than through a vendor-owned .cz property. This is exactly the language asymmetry the cell rationale predicted.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms the collection design: monitor global vendor newsrooms in EN, and monitor Czech-language pickup separately via Protext and the trade press. Do not expect a vendor-owned Czech newsroom to exist.

negative_findings.description: Two vendor case-study libraries were read in full and neither contains a Czech customer. Diebold Nixdorf's banking case studies currently list Bankart, IPAK YULI Bank (Uzbekistan), GHS Federal Credit Union, Cooperative Bank of Kielce (Poland), America First Credit Union, Banca Raiffeisen Locarno (Switzerland) and JN Bank. NCR Atleos's Customer Stories are almost entirely US credit unions with Santander UK as the only European entry.
negative_findings.result_summary: By contrast Temenos does carry a Czech reference (Komerční banka, both a selection release and a go-live release plus a success story). So the Czech reference asymmetry across vendors is real and measurable.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: This is a genuine competitor-positioning finding, not just an absence: on their own public evidence, Temenos has a marquee Czech core-banking reference while Diebold Nixdorf and NCR Atleos publicise none. It also means the case-study libraries are worth monitoring as tripwires rather than as current sources of Czech content.

negative_findings.description: A consistent WAF/bot-defence pattern blocked six otherwise-central sources from this fetcher: Finastra press-media (403 on three path variants), Printec Group (403 on three paths), Asseco Central Europe at ce.asseco.com (403), Finextra retail-banking channel (403), SEC EDGAR full-text and browse-edgar endpoints (403, User-Agent policy), and Fiserv newsroom (two 60s timeouts). Thales Group's corporate press-release page returned an empty document body on two path variants, consistent with client-side rendering or a consent gate.
negative_findings.result_summary: NONE of these is recorded as dead. 403-with-no-body and repeated timeouts are the signature of edge bot rules, and in SEC's case the 403 is documented policy for clients that do not declare a contact User-Agent. Euronet is a separate case: a 301 from euronetworldwide.com/news to euronet.com/news that itself 404s indicates a site migration, i.e. moved.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The collection layer for this cell must be provisioned with a headless browser and realistic headers, plus a compliant declaring User-Agent for SEC. Without that, roughly a third of the cell's highest-value sources will look permanently unavailable when they are merely defended.

negative_findings.description: Lupa.cz was fetched and assessed as a candidate Czech-language channel and deliberately NOT included. It is a Czech internet/technology portal whose visible content on the day of assessment covered AI, healthcare digitisation, cloud infrastructure, 3D printing and quantum computing, with no banking IT, fintech or payments coverage in evidence, and no RSS link visible.
negative_findings.result_summary: Rejected for this cell on relevance grounds rather than reachability. Bankovnictví online and SystemOnLine cover the same country with far higher banking-technology density.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Documents a deliberate exclusion so a later run does not re-litigate it, and keeps the candidate list precision-weighted rather than padded.

negative_findings.description: NCR Atleos's own investor newsroom carries the release 'Shareholders Overwhelmingly Vote to Approve Brink's Acquisition of NCR Atleos' dated 30 June 2026, alongside Q2 2026 results dated 5 August 2026.
negative_findings.result_summary: The investor.ncratleos.com domain, its RSS feed and its numeric /detail/<id>/ archive are all at material risk of retirement or redirection into Brink's investor infrastructure once the transaction closes.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: This is the single best-automatable endpoint in the cell (real RSS, stable IDs). If it is not mirrored before close, the historical ATM-vendor announcement archive for CEE could become materially harder to reconstruct, and a live monitor would silently go quiet rather than error.

coverage_gaps.description: Zero search-engine queries were executed for this cell (WebSearch budget pre-exhausted; DuckDuckGo CAPTCHA, Mojeek 403, Bing RSS cache-collided). Every candidate here was reached by domain reasoning, direct navigation or on-site search, so the long tail of vendors and the entire class of 'sources I did not already know to guess' is unexplored.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Re-run cell #17 with a restored search budget and execute all six assigned seed queries plus the cs variants verbatim, then diff the resulting candidate set against this slice to measure what domain-reasoning alone missed.

coverage_gaps.description: Named-but-unreached in this pass: Fiserv (timeout), Finastra (403), Printec (403), Thales Group corporate (empty body), Euronet (path migrated). Reasoned-about but never fetched at all: ACI Worldwide (aciworldwide.com/news-and-events 301s to investor.aciworldwide.com/events-and-presentations; the news-releases path then timed out), Worldline (two path guesses 404'd), NCR Voyix, Nexi, Backbase, Mambu, Thought Machine, Sopra Banking Software, Tietoevry, Hyosung TCS, GRGBanking, KAL ATM Software, Cennox, IDEMIA, Giesecke+Devrient, BS/2 (Penki kontinentai), Asseco SEE.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a second pass dedicated to resolving canonical newsroom/IR paths for this list, using a headless browser and following redirect chains rather than guessing paths. Prioritise ACI Worldwide, Worldline, BS/2 and Hyosung as the most CEE-plausible of the unreached set.

coverage_gaps.description: The earnings-call TRANSCRIPT channel — explicitly named in this cell's rationale as where vendors mention country deployments — has no source assigned. IR pages give decks and webcast links, but searchable transcript text (where a CFO says 'Czech Republic' in Q&A) sits with third parties: Motley Fool, Seeking Alpha, Quartr, AlphaSense, Koyfin, and the vendors' own webcast providers. None was evaluated.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Evaluate transcript providers for licence terms and machine access, and decide between (a) licensed transcript feeds, (b) speech-to-text over the vendors' own public webcast audio, which avoids third-party copyright entirely, or (c) manual review of the four or five most CZ-relevant issuers' quarterly calls. Option (b) is the cleanest legally.

coverage_gaps.description: Vendor LinkedIn newsrooms and regional/country LinkedIn pages are unassessed. For this cell they matter disproportionately: CEE country organisations and local sales teams frequently post a Czech customer win on LinkedIn that never reaches the global newsroom, and LinkedIn is the practical fallback for the vendors whose own sites are WAF-blocked (Finastra, Printec). Vendor LinkedIn URLs were observed on Diebold Nixdorf, Temenos, Comarch, Bankovnictví and Protext pages but none was evaluated.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Assess LinkedIn company-page monitoring for the cell's vendor list under LinkedIn's terms of service; if automated collection is not permissible, define a manual monthly review of the 8-10 most CZ-relevant vendor pages plus their Czech/CEE country pages.

coverage_gaps.description: Czech-language coverage rests on exactly three verified portals (Protext, Bankovnictví online, SystemOnLine) and no cs-language keyword search was ever executed against any index. Nine constructed Czech terms remain unexercised: platební terminál, jádrový bankovní systém, samoobslužná zóna, recyklace hotovosti, výroční zpráva, případová studie, nasazení, implementace, dodavatel.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: With a restored search budget, run each unexercised cs term against a search engine AND against the Protext /vyhledavani/ endpoint, paired with each global vendor name, and add whatever new Czech-language channels surface. Also probe for Czech-language aggregators of foreign corporate news that were not reachable in this pass.

coverage_gaps.description: Only three machine-friendly feeds were confirmed across the entire cell: NCR Atleos IR RSS, Auriga /en/feed/, and ATM Marketplace /rss/. Global Payments IR advertises an RSS feed. Everything else is JS-rendered (Diebold Nixdorf IR), WAF-gated, or offers no feed at all (FIS media room showed none).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Provision the collector with a headless-browser tier and a compliant declaring User-Agent for SEC before this cell goes live; otherwise budget for HTML-diff scraping on Temenos, FIS, NCR Atleos corporate, Diebold Nixdorf and the Czech portals, and treat the four known feeds as the only low-cost paths.

coverage_gaps.description: The NCR Atleos investor archive (RSS plus numeric /detail/<id>/ URLs) is exposed to the pending Brink's acquisition, and the Euronet news path has already migrated in a way that broke its own redirect (301 to a 404). No snapshotting has been done for either.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Mirror the full investor.ncratleos.com press-release archive immediately, before transaction close, and register a successor watch on Brink's investor relations. Re-resolve Euronet's live IR path and prefer EDGAR-by-CIK collection for Euronet so the source survives further site migrations.

brief: For Czech references, this cell's source landscape is sharply uneven: Temenos is the one global vendor with a verified, well-structured Czech trail — Komerční banka selection and go-live press releases plus a success story, all English-only, all reachable through a newsroom with Region/Category/Year filters and a working on-site search — while Diebold Nixdorf's and NCR Atleos's public case-study libraries carry no Czech customer at all, which is itself the competitor-positioning evidence the cell was created to produce. The best-automatable endpoints are NCR Atleos's investor RSS, Auriga's feed and ATM Marketplace's feed, but the Atleos archive is at real risk from the pending Brink's acquisition and should be mirrored now; a further six central sources (Finastra, Printec, Asseco CE, Finextra, Fiserv, SEC EDGAR) returned 403s or timeouts that read as bot defences rather than dead links, so this cell needs a headless-browser collector and a declaring User-Agent for SEC before it goes live. Local-language reality is that no global vendor in this cell runs a Czech-language site — the Diebold Nixdorf cs-cz path 500s, comarch.cz is parked, printec.cz fails TLS — so Czech-language pickup has to be caught downstream at ČTK's Protext wire and in the Czech trade press (Bankovnictví online, IT Systems/SystemOnLine), all three verified live. The whole slice was produced without a single search-engine query because the session's WebSearch budget was already exhausted and every fallback engine blocked or cache-collided, so treat it as high-precision, deliberately incomplete on recall, and worth re-running against a live index.
